model: A seed fails if any per-seed breach gate of the design fails or lacks evidence (fewer acquisitions than the minimum); a plan is rejected if more than floor(10% × seeds) seeds fail.
Exact: independent studies; each seed's volume is Poisson at a daily rate spread evenly over the range; every seed at the planning rates (urgent as given).

Monte Carlo: 40 seeds; each seed's underlying rate is beta-distributed around the planning rate with SD seedSD (scaled by rate ÷ urgent planning rate for soon and routine); each week's rate is beta-distributed around the seed's with intra-week correlation weeklyICC; volumes Poisson per week at a rate drawn uniformly from the range. Deterministic PCG streams.
Pooled gates are not modelled: with 40 seeds their counts are far larger and pass at the planning rates.

clusterModel: Per seed, a 150-day gated period (T90 = days 1-90, tail = days 91-150), each priority's daily volume Poisson at a rate drawn uniformly from dailyVolume, times the weekday profile (Mon 1.1, Tue-Fri 1, Sat 0.25, Sun 0, scaled to a mean of 1) and a gamma day factor (dailyVolumeCV) where the model says so.
Breach probability: each Monday-based week's rate beta-distributed around the setting's rate with intra-week correlation weekICC; each day's around the week's with intra-day correlation dayICC.

The per-seed gates exactly as the policy (urgent over the gated period; soon and routine in T90 and the tail; evidence minimums). Seeds are independent and alike, so an evaluation's rejection is P(Binomial(seeds, perSeedFailure) > floor(10% x seeds)).

The dependence range is bounded by the development diagnostics (docs/calibration/policy-5c2/clustering.md); no threshold, window or allowance was chosen from them. Deterministic PCG streams; regenerate with DT_OC=1.

model: A reading queue simulated hour by hour from the takeover (Tue 2026-10-13 06:00) for 181 days (internal/eval/oc_queue_test.go): 52 acquisitions a day (Poisson; the weekday profile; 08:00-20:00), 2% urgent, 12% soon, 86% routine; reading Mon-Fri 07:30-20:00 and Sat 10:00-14:00 at a utilization of 0.85 of the season-1 demand, urgent first, then soon, then routine, first in first out. Daily samples at 06:00; the record's horizon is day 150, so the reference block is days 55-82 and the later blocks 83-110, 111-138 and 139-166 (covering).

Seasonal scenarios multiply demand by the scenario's monthly season factor; bursty ones by a gamma day factor of the stated CV; capacity scenarios multiply reading capacity on the stated days; inherited work is acquired before the takeover and not read until the stated day; held-back work joins the queue the stated days after its acquisition.
Each seed is judged by judgeBacklog under each rule. A rule's rejection at S seeds is P(Binomial(S, unstable fraction) > floor(10% x S)).

T1: every stable scenario's rejection at 40 seeds at most 0.05. T2: every deteriorating scenario's unstable fraction at least 0.90. Selection among the candidates meeting both: the highest mean unstable fraction on the ladder (L5, L10), then the protocol's tie-break order (the family's order). Ladder and sensitivity scenarios are reported, not targets.
